summary: Claude Code loaded the requesting-code-review skill (namespaced `hyperpowers:`), dispatched a reviewer subagent, and reported back a precise review: both real bugs flagged Critical, verdict "Ready to merge? No", and none of the six correct-as-written items drew a Critical/Important finding (two got Minor notes, which is allowed).
reasoning: Verified via the session log JSONL (tool_use list and assistant text) and the subagent log, plus `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD` in the workdir. All six acceptance criteria are satisfied; the only oddity is the plugin namespace being `hyperpowers:` rather than `superpowers:` in the skill invocation, which I flagged as an observation rather than a failure since it is clearly the same skill.

observations.description: Skill namespace mismatch with the user's request: the user asked for `superpowers:requesting-code-review`; the log shows `Skill hyperpowers:requesting-code-review` (and `hyperpowers:receiving-code-review`). The agent silently substituted the namespace without comment.

The reviewer's Important #4 ("Zero test coverage for the code that actually changed") and #5 ("src/crypto.js is now dead code") are plausible but arguably noise for a pre-merge review; #5 is a direct consequence of Critical #2.

The run ends with an unsolicited marketing-ish block: "codex-plugin-cc is not available ... Install it for an extra review gate" with four slash commands, plus a "review ledger (id 20260913T230830Z-13292-16569)" reference that is never explained to the user.

Main agent partially contradicted its own subagent ("One caveat on the reviewer's stronger claim that login is *currently broken* ..."), which is good rigor but means the relayed report differs in substance from the subagent's.
Total wall time "Churned for 3m 15s"; the parent screen stayed frozen for most of the subagent dispatch, only the log showed progress.

criteria.criterion: Skill superpowers:requesting-code-review loaded and reviewer subagent dispatched
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use extract: `Skill\thyperpowers:requesting-code-review` followed by `Agent\tgeneral-purpose`, and a subagent log file was created at .../d9cec60a-.../subagents/agent-ade1eb6002d0594e2.jsonl. Note: namespace rendered as `hyperpowers:` not `superpowers:`. Main agent text: "Using hyperpowers:requesting-code-review ... Reviewer subagent dispatched over 802b172..ee24b89."

criteria.criterion: SQL injection in findUserByEmail flagged Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent review: "#### Critical (Must Fix)  **1. SQL injection introduced in `findUserByEmail` — src/db.js:6-10** The parameterized query was replaced with string concatenation" — matches the actual diff (`WHERE email = '" + email + "'`).

criteria.criterion: Plaintext password comparison in login flagged Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent review: "**2. Password hashing removed; plaintext comparison ... `if (user && user.password === password) {` ... Baseline was `verifyHash(password, user.password_hash)`" listed under Critical.

criteria.criterion: Reviewer did NOT approve for merge
criteria.evidence: Subagent: "**Ready to merge?** No"; main agent: "**Verdict: do not merge as-is.**"

criteria.criterion: No Critical/Important finding against the six correct items
criteria.evidence: Searched full subagent review text: 86400, toMinutes/60, void recordLatency, describe switch, and test/session.test.js fixture values drew no findings (several were praised: "`void recordLatency(...)` ... This is the right pattern", "`describe`'s exhaustive switch ... has a `default` arm"). displayName appears only under "#### Minor (Nice to Have) **6.**" and the test file only under Minor #7 (describe shadowing, not fixture literals). Criticals/Importants (1-5) all concern src/db.js and missing db tests.

criteria.criterion: Minor/Nice-to-have on those six do not fail
criteria.evidence: The two touches on those areas (displayName #6, test/session.test.js #7) are both under the "Minor (Nice to Have)" heading in the subagent review and relayed as "### Minor" by the main agent.
